findings.evidence: roadmap/EpsilonEridaniRoadmaps/SpinStructure/README.md:395 `(M/(p·q)) · G.g1 x Q² · E₁  +  (1/(M (p·q))) · G.g2 x Q² · E₂`; code line 200-201 `(√(K.M2 g) / g K.p K.q * g₁) • … + (√(K.M2 g) / g K.p K.q ^ 2 * g₂) • …`.
findings.fix: Use `(1 / (√(K.M2 g) * g K.p K.q) * g₂) • spinStructureTwo ε K` and update `fromG1G2_apply`, `IsG1G2Decomposition.apply` and all five docstring occurrences; or, if the deviation is deliberate, say so explicitly and justify it against the roadmap formula.
findings.issue: `fromG1G2`'s second coefficient is `√(K.M2 g) / g K.p K.q ^ 2 * g₂`, i.e. `M/(p·q)²`. Roadmap §0.2 (README.md:395) and the PR description both specify `1/(M (p·q))`; these differ by `M²/(p·q)`, so `StructureFunctions.g2` means something other than the roadmap's `g₂` in the public predicate `IsG1G2Decomposition`, and every later stage (0.3 σ_LT′, 0.4 A₁/A₂ relations) inherits it. The same wrong factor is restated in the docstrings at lines 29, 194, 206-207, 255 and in `IsG1G2Decomposition.apply` (283).

findings.evidence: Lines 196-198 and 29; `spinStructureTwo` (95-96) is `ε.bilinMap ![K.q, g K.p K.q • K.S - g K.S K.q • K.p]`, i.e. `(p·q)·ε(·,·,q,S_⊥)`.
findings.fix: Correct the coefficient per the previous finding, after which the "standard form" sentence becomes true; otherwise drop the claim.
findings.issue: The `fromG1G2` docstring calls `(M / (p·q)) · ε(·, ·, q, g₁ S + g₂ (S − ((S·q)/(p·q)) p))` "the standard form of the spin-dependent hadronic tensor". With `E₂ = (p·q) ε(·,·,q,S_⊥)`, the standard `1/(M(p·q))` coefficient gives `(1/M) ε(·,·,q,S_⊥)`, not `(M/(p·q)) ε(·,·,q,S_⊥)`. A consumer reading the docstring will assume the literature normalisation and get a different `g₂`.

findings.evidence: Lines 270-298 list the whole namespace; `fromG1G2_reverse` at 236-241; `Polarized/Kinematics.lean:86-87 reverse_toDisKinematics … := (rfl)`.

findings.issue: `IsG1G2Decomposition`'s elimination API covers `eq`/`apply`/`isAlt`/`conserved_left`/`conserved_right` but not `PolarizedKinematics.reverse`, the one operation in scope that the file develops for `spinStructureOne/Two` and `fromG1G2`. A consumer holding `h : IsG1G2Decomposition ε K G W` and wanting the spin-reversed tensor (what 0.3's σ_TT′/σ_LT′ cross-section differences compare) must go through `h.eq` and `fromG1G2_reverse` by hand.

findings.evidence: Lines 152/163/236 carry `@[simp]`; 178-188 and 243-248 do not. `grep -n 'spinStructureOne_smul\|spinStructureOne_add' Tensor.lean` has no hit.

findings.issue: `spinStructureOne_neg`, `spinStructureTwo_neg` (185) and `fromG1G2_neg` (244) are normal-form lemmas pushing the sign out of `ε`, exactly parallel to the `_reverse` trio, but carry no `@[simp]` while all three `_reverse` lemmas do (152, 163, 236). Also, the module docstring (44-46) asserts "Both structures are linear in `ε`" while only the `neg` instance is available — there is no `_add`/`_smul` in `ε`.

summary: The prior round's gaps (named witness, `.eq`/`.apply`, reverse interaction, diagonal simp lemmas) are all closed. What remains: `fromG1G2`'s `g₂` coefficient is not the roadmap's (nor the PR description's), making the docstring's "standard form" claim false; `IsG1G2Decomposition` has no `reverse` elimination although the file develops `reverse` for everything else; the `_neg` trio is unannotated where the parallel `_reverse` trio is `@[simp]`.
